system.name: FairQueue
system.one_liner: Shows that prompt learning for fair text-to-image generation (ITI-GEN) degrades image quality, then fixes it with prompt queuing and attention amplification.

content.variant_note: three tinted bands (observation, analysis, proposed solution) of three titled panels each; grey block arrows link panels, and plus and equals signs join the last band
content.argues: ITI-GEN's learned prompts distort images because the reference-image direction carries unrelated concepts; attention analysis shows early-step damage, and queuing the prompts plus amplifying attention fixes quality.
content.subject: A nine-panel argument: degraded samples, reference photos and CLIP-space geometry; attention maps, prompt switching and histograms; then the two-part fix with result bars.

elements.name: I2H
elements.role: switches the prompt from ITI-GEN prompt P in steps 0 to n-1 to hard prompt F in steps n to l

elements.name: H2I

elements.name: Cross Attention
elements.role: the denoising network of the T2I model, run for l steps

elements.name: Prompt Queuing

elements.name: Attention Amplification

lessons.what_to_learn: Stack an analysis paper's argument as tinted bands (observation, analysis, solution) with three titled panels each, link panels with block arrows, and close with plus and equals signs so the fix and its results read as one equation.
lessons.suits: analysis-driven papers that diagnose a failure of prior work in several steps (samples, geometry, internals) before presenting a fix with results.

evidence: (a) We observe degradation in images generated through ITI-GEN’s learned prompts.
prompt queuing first utilizes T in the early n denoising steps, thereby allowing for the global structures to form properly
Our results in Fig. 1a (col3) shows the directional loss between ∆I and ∆F

summary: FairQueue revisits prompt learning for fair text-to-image generation (ITI-GEN), shows that its learned prompts degrade image quality, and fixes this with prompt queuing and attention amplification. Figure 1 is a three-band story on tinted ground. Band (a) Observation shows a mosaic of degraded ITI-GEN faces, the reference photos used to learn prompts and a CLIP-space sphere whose ΔI, ΔP and ΔF vectors explain a directional-loss table. Band (b) Analysis shows token attention maps for the hard prompt and ITI-GEN, a prompt-switching denoiser (I2H, H2I) and histograms. Band (c) Proposed Solution shows Prompt Queuing plus Attention Amplification equals bar-chart Results against ITI-GEN. Grey block arrows link panels.
summary_zh: FairQueue 重新审视公平文生图的提示学习方法 ITI-GEN，指出其提示会降低画质，并提出提示排队与注意力放大。图 1 分为观察、分析、解决方案三个色带共九个面板，含退化样本、CLIP 空间示意、注意力图、直方图和结果柱状图。
notes: Prior labels had contribution-mosaic first; arrows, plus and equals signs run through the panels, so the figure is read as problem-then-fix with a concept-schematic and a model-anatomy panel. Which of the black and blue denoiser outputs belongs to I2H or H2I is not keyed in the figure; the blue frame and arc only match the H2I box. The histograms look like exported plotting-library bitmaps (their tick labels are absent from the text layer); the Results bars are vector.
